page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a constrained-vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting standard instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and FMA, but lacking AVX-512 extensions. The instance is allocated 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware resources include 275 GB of local SSD storage, while dedicated GPU accelerators are omitted entirely.

Benchmark results highlight the memory-centric profile alongside moderate compute performance. In compute evaluations, the instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1604.0, a multi-core score of 6375.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 11895.86, all falling within the middle 50% category. In contrast, stress-ng multi-core testing reached 3060.15 (bottom 25%) and single-core testing reached 763.78 (bottom 10%), indicating limited raw compute execution relative to denser CPU offerings. Small-block cached memory bandwidth read-only throughput achieved 515.14 GB/sec (middle 50%), though uncached large-block operations demonstrated lower bandwidth, with read speeds at 39.27 GB/sec and write speeds at 22.62 GB/sec. Operational throughput benchmarks remained consistent, showing 8.29 million operations/sec on Redis SET workloads and 10.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The constrained CPU structure provides a distinct architectural tradeoff, trading raw core count for a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. This profile lowers compute-bound licensing overheads while preserving substantial system RAM. However, the lack of AVX-512 extensions and dedicated accelerators results in low LLM inference performance, where text generation for medium 7B models reached only 6.29 tokens/sec (bottom 10%). The Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is strategically suited for memory-intensive workloads that require moderate compute resources, including in-memory caches, relational database systems, enterprise ERP systems, and batch data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine offering 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor alongside 128.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU, 275 GB of local SSD storage, and no GPU hardware. In performance testing, it exhibits solid general operational marks, logging 8.29 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, a Geekbench multi-core score of 6375.0, and cached read memory bandwidth reaching 515.14 GB/sec. Compute-dense and vector workloads show clear limits due to the constrained core architecture and absence of AVX-512, reflected in weak stress-ng multi-core execution (3060.15) and slow 7B LLM inference (6.29 tokens/sec). By maintaining high memory allocations on a reduced core count, the server is well aligned for database hosting, in-memory caching, and memory-heavy enterprise applications.
